playbook:
When I'm dealt KING and I am to act first, I bet to build the pot and apply pressure.
When I'm dealt KING and my opponent checks to me, I bet for value.
When I'm dealt KING and my opponent bets into me, I call a single-chip bet (play K aggressively; don't fold K to one chip).
When I'm dealt QUEEN and I am to act first, I usually bet to protect and apply pressure.
When I'm dealt QUEEN and my opponent checks to me, I bet to try to take the pot.
When I'm dealt QUEEN and my opponent bets into me, I call a single-chip bet (don't fold Q to a one-chip bet).
When I'm dealt JACK and I am to act first, I default to checking (avoid bluffing as opener).
When I'm dealt JACK and my opponent checks to me, I only bluff very rarely; do not bluff with J routinely.
When I'm dealt JACK and my opponent bets into me, I fold to protect chips unless pot odds or a specific read strongly justify calling.
Always declare my actual card truthfully at showdown.
